test_title: PYST 13 - SSC CHSL 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 17 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A savings scheme offers compound interest annually. A woman deposits ₹10,000. At the end of the first year, the interest rate is 10%. In the second year, due to inflation, the interest rate rises to 12.5%, and in the third year, it drops to 8%. Calculate the total interest she earned at the end of 3 years.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Successive Multiplier** method for varying interest rates.

Multiplier for Year 1 (10%) = 1.1, Year 2 (12.5%) = 1.125, Year 3 (8%) = 1.08

Total Multiplier = 1.1 × 1.125 × 1.08 = 1.3365

Total Interest = Principal × (Total Multiplier − 1) = 10,000 × 0.3365 = ₹3,365

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,365.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹10,000

**Rate (Year 1)** = 10%, **Rate (Year 2)** = 12.5%, **Rate (Year 3)** = 8%

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100) × (1 + r₃/100)

Compound Interest (CI) = Amount − Principal

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/543f8d3730ff15215f096cbde35742136786073bbfd6e218060cc7ef4ba56484.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount at end of Year 1 = 10,000 × (110/100) = ₹11,000

⇒ Amount at end of Year 2 = 11,000 × (112.5/100) = 11,000 × (9/8) = ₹12,375

⇒ Amount at end of Year 3 = 12,375 × (108/100) = 12,375 × (27/25) = ₹13,365

⇒ Total Interest = Final Amount − Initial Principal

⇒ Total Interest = 13,365 − 10,000 = ₹3,365

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,365.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest with Different Rates

When interest rates vary annually, the amount is calculated as A = P(1 + r₁/100)(1 + r₂/100)...(1 + rₙ/100).

Fractional Equivalents for Speed

Using fractions like 12.5% = 1/8 (multiplier 9/8) and 8% = 2/25 (multiplier 27/25) simplifies the **calculation** of compound growth significantly.

Effective Percentage Rate

The total effective rate for successive percentages a%, b%, and c% is [ (1 + a/100)(1 + b/100)(1 + c/100) − 1 ] × 100.
